headline: Daily rental prices for humanoid robots in China have fallen from five-figure yuan sums to under 1,000 yuan as dedicated rental exchanges appear, Notebookcheck reports.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a market signal on humanoid robots, but the figures come from listings and an unnamed report, and much of it dates from early 2026.
importance_line: Cheaper rentals make it easier for businesses and curious customers to try a humanoid for a day, but many rentals are for shows and exhibitions, the prices come from listings and an unnamed report, and it is unclear whether cheaper rental leads to real work.
summary: Notebookcheck reports, citing a recent report it does not name, that daily rental rates for humanoid robots in China, which reportedly reached five figures in yuan (about 1,400 dollars or more) after Unitree's robots danced at the 2025 Spring Festival Gala, fell to 2,000 to 3,000 yuan by early 2026 and have since dropped below 1,000 yuan, with some Unitree units listed from 289 yuan (about 40 dollars) a day. It puts the slide down to more robots in circulation and a fading novelty premium, and notes that Qingtianzu, billed as the first dedicated robot rental platform, announced a seed funding round in January 2026.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text; page dated 10 Oct 2026. The 'newest report' behind the figures is not named, and the early-2026 data points are older than the article. Price levels are reported, not independently checked.
